Updated November 23, 2026: Bring Your Own Telephony (BYOT) is now generally available. We've updated this post with BYOT details.

Updated October 30, 2026: We have updated this post with additional information as the feature is now generally available. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) and Bring Your Own Telephony Provider (BYOT) are now generally available in Microsoft Entra ID. Both connect Microsoft Entra to a telephony provider through an integration in your Azure subscription, but you purchase and deploy them differently. Microsoft Entra continues to manage the authentication experience, including one-time passcode (OTP) generation and validation, and your provider delivers the SMS messages and voice calls. 

  • CYOT is the recommended option when a supported offering meets your coverage, contractual and compliance requirements. It gives you providers evaluated by Microsoft for geographic coverage and fraud protection, purchasing through Microsoft Security Store, billing through your Azure subscription and guided deployment in the Microsoft Entra admin center. 
  • BYOT is for cases where an existing provider agreement or a specific requirement can't be met by the supported CYOT offerings. You get your provider's ready-to-deploy integration package, set up your account directly with the provider, and configure the integration through APIs. 

With either option, your organization owns the Azure resources in your subscription and your telephony provider account. 

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication starts retiring on February 1, 2027. If your users need SMS or voice after that date, set up CYOT or BYOT before then. 

Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, instead of SMS or voice. Use a telephony provider only for user groups that have a business, regulatory or technical need for telephony-based authentication.

What you need to do

If your organization needs to keep SMS or voice authentication: 

  1. Identify users who need SMS or voice. Confirm which users have a requirement that phishing-resistant methods can't meet. 
  2. Choose your option and provider. Review CYOT and BYOT. Use CYOT when a supported provider meets your coverage, contractual and compliance requirements. Otherwise, use BYOT. 
  3. Check prerequisites. You need an Azure subscription with a valid payment method to host the integration, plus the Owner role or Contributor plus Role Based Access Control Administrator. For CYOT, the subscription must also be eligible for Security Store purchases. 
  4. Estimate costs. Review provider pricing and Azure hosting costs. 
  5. Set up and roll out. Follow the setup guide for CYOT or BYOT. Start in evaluation mode, then move traffic to your provider in stages. 
  6. Complete your transition before February 1, 2027. Review the guidance for the retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication.
